headline: Elementary school building planners favored a $38M Neary School renovation, while committees advanced golf irrigation funding and 2027 tricentennial plans.
synopsis: Architects advised the Elementary School Building Committee that a $15 million base repair of Neary School would net only $5.8 million in direct construction after mandatory code upgrades, prompting the committee to advance a $38 million addition-renovation plan. The Golf Committee finalized its strategy for Special Town Meeting to pursue extended and additional Community Preservation Act funds for course irrigation, while voting to fund an Audubon environmental consultant. Southborough tricentennial organizers executed a contract for a 200-drone aerial light show to launch the town 300th anniversary on New Year's Day 2027. Additionally, the Board of Health granted a septic variance for a residential conversion on Breakneck Hill Road and noted that seasonal flu vaccine supplies are nearly depleted.

highlights.title: Neary School renovation options and cost analysis
highlights.why: Architects demonstrated that a $15 million upgrade nets only $5.8 million in direct construction due to code-mandated accessibility and sprinkler work, leading planners to favor a $38 million addition and renovation plan.

highlights.title: Golf course irrigation funding warrant article
highlights.why: The committee organized its advocacy for Special Town Meeting to extend $550,000 in expiring Community Preservation Act funds and seek roughly $350,000 in new CPA funding plus $100,000 from revolving funds.

highlights.title: Tricentennial drone show contract and kickoff plans
highlights.why: The town executed a contract with Firefly for a 200-drone light show on January 1, 2027, featuring custom formations including artwork designed by local middle school students.

highlights.title: Septic variance for 66 Breakneck Hill Road
highlights.why: The Board of Health unanimously approved an 85-foot wetland setback variance to allow converting a commercial building into a four-bedroom single-family home using advanced nitrogen-reducing treatment.

highlights.title: Audubon certification dues and consultant funding
highlights.why: The committee voted to pay $500 in membership dues and authorized up to $4,500 from its revolving account to hire an environmental consultant to complete the golf course certification process.

highlights.title: Town flu vaccine supplies nearly depleted
highlights.why: Health officials reported that town-run influenza vaccination clinics are concluding with remaining supplies limited to two schools, two daycares, and emergency personnel as seasonal flu cases emerge.
